symbols.name: chirp vector
symbols.meaning: The vector of chirp factors whose entry at each integer tau is e^{pi i tau^2/q}.
symbols.quote: The chirp is the vector $\chi$ whose entry at each integer $\tau$ is $\chi_\tau = e^{\pi i \tau^2/q}$.

symbols.name: chirp position
symbols.meaning: The integer position of a chirp entry, which may be negative or larger than q-1.
symbols.quote: Here $\tau$ is the integer position of a chirp entry, which may be negative or larger than $q-1$.

symbols.name: rescaled input vector
symbols.meaning: The vector whose entry j is the input entry u_j divided by the chirp entry chi_j.
symbols.quote: Write $\hat u = \frac{1}{\chi}\cdot u$, so $\hat u_j = u_j/\chi_j$.

symbols.name: remainder modulo q
symbols.meaning: x mod q is the remainder of the integer x on division by q, a position in {0,...,q-1}.
symbols.quote: Here $x \bmod q$ denotes the remainder of the integer $x$ on division by $q$, the position in $\{0,\dots,q-1\}$ reached by $x$ on a cycle of $q$ positions.

relations.quote: Bluestein's chirp identity rewrites the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) $F_q$ as a convolution multiplied by chirp factors.
It reduces the transform to a [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md), so any method that computes that convolution also computes the transform.
In the paper, it converts the middle transform into a [normalized cyclic convolution](normalized-cyclic-convolution.md).
The identity keeps the target permutation of the [transform identity with retained permutations](transform-identity.md) inside the formula, so that it is never executed as a separate sort.
The transform's cost bound is stated in terms of the [logarithm](logarithm.md) $\lg$ to base 2, because it is that of the convolution plus $O(q)$.
